Topics · The holy books together

Does God forgive freely when I come back?

In Jesus' parable the father runs to his lost son. The Quran asks what a returner owes, and who must pay.

Part 1 of 3

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

In Luke's Gospel Jesus tells of a son who takes his share, spends it and comes home with a speech prepared. His father sees him from far off and runs. The embrace comes before the speech, and a robe, a ring and a feast cut it short. Look for what the father asked and you find one thing: the son came. The verse speaks to the same person, one who has wasted himself, and says despair is the only thing left to give up, because God forgives all sins.

A question for you

Go back over the story in your mind. What did the father ask of his son before the embrace?

If you sayNothing. He ran first
ThenThen the embrace came before any word of regret reached him. The son's only act was turning for home. Keep that in view when the next verse names what turning is.
If you sayThat he come back and admit his wrong
ThenThe son does both, and the father receives them. Notice that the confession is no price, since the embrace came before the words. The next verse names what a returning person does.
If you sayThe story leaves that out; the cost is paid elsewhere
ThenThis is how many Christians hear it: the parable shows the welcome, the cross shows what the welcome cost. Let that stand, and read on.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَـٰحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُوا۟ لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَن يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُوا۟ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allāh and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allāh? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:135

Translation

Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness.

Original · Hebrew

מִי־אֵ֣ל כָּמ֗וֹךָ נֹשֵׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְעֹבֵ֣ר עַל־פֶּ֔שַׁע לִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית נַחֲלָת֑וֹ לֹא־הֶחֱזִ֤יק לָעַד֙ אַפּ֔וֹ כִּֽי־חָפֵ֥ץ חֶ֖סֶד הֽוּא׃

Micah · 7:18

World English Bible

Coming back has a shape. The verse lists it: having done wrong, people remember God, ask forgiveness and do not knowingly carry on. In the middle it asks who forgives sins except God. The son in the story does these things: he comes to himself, he gets up, he says he has sinned, he does not go back to the far country. Both texts show a person coming straight back, and forgiveness coming from God.

A question for you

Which of these steps do you find hardest?

If you sayRemembering God when I have done wrong
ThenThat is the step shame blocks. The verse puts it first, so the way back begins with a single thought.
If you sayAsking to be forgiven
ThenTo ask is to admit there is someone to ask, and that the debt is real. The verse puts that in your own mouth.
If you sayNot going back to it
ThenThat is the long step, and the verse counts it as part of the return. It speaks of those who do not persist knowingly, which leaves room for someone who stumbles and turns again.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِى رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ ۚ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Is it other than Allāh I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:164

Translation

The soul who sins, he shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be on him.

Original · Hebrew

הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א ׀ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת הָרָשָׁ֖ע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

Ezekiel · 18:20

World English Bible

﴿فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words,[22] and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of Repentance,[23] the Merciful.

Translator's notes

[22] Allāh taught Adam words of repentance that would be acceptable to Him. [23] Literally, He who perpetually returns, i.e., reminding and enabling His servant to repent from sins and then forgiving him. Thus, He is also the constant motivator of the repentance He accepts.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:37

Translation

Take words with you, and return to Yahweh. Tell him, “Forgive all our sins, and accept that which is good; so we offer bulls as we vowed of our lips.

Original · Hebrew

קְח֤וּ עִמָּכֶם֙ דְּבָרִ֔ים וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה אִמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כָּל־תִּשָּׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְקַח־ט֔וֹב וּֽנְשַׁלְּמָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים שְׂפָתֵֽינוּ׃

Hosea · 14:2

World English Bible

Now the second half of the question. Christians hold that God is just, that sin is real, and that God Himself bore the cost in love at the cross. The verse gives its own principle: no one carries another's load. So ask what forgiving means. When a creditor forgives, no one pays the debt. It is let go, and the letting go is what he bears. The second verse shows this in Adam: he received words, and God turned to him.

A question for you

When you forgive someone who wronged you, who carries the cost?

If you sayI do; forgiving is mine to give
ThenThen you have described forgiveness as the one wronged letting go. The verses show God's forgiveness wider still.
If you sayHuman forgiveness differs; God is holy and just
ThenThat is a deep concern, held with reverence. The verses show justice and mercy together: each soul answers for itself, and the one who returns is welcomed. Weigh this in your heart and mind.
If you sayGod bore the cost Himself in Christ
ThenThis is the heart of Christian faith, and it is said with love. For you the one forgiving and the one suffering are the same. Christians and Muslims meet in this: God forgives. Here each person weighs for themselves.

The same in the other books

Translation

“In those days they will say no more, “‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’ But everyone will die for his own iniquity. Every man who eats the sour grapes, his teeth will be set on edge.

Jeremiah · 31:29-30

World English Bible

Translation

Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.

חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי׃ הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 51:1-2

World English Bible

Translation

Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him. If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”

προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ· καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.

the Gospel (Luke) · 17:3-4

World English Bible
